summary:
Our project has concluded with a creation of a website that finds a set of best earth analog locations for a chosen point on a surface of moon/mars based on 10 indicators. For maximum flexibility, the user may change the lunar/martian time in which the mission will take place, and assign individually chosen values of importance for imitating every one of the indicators best. 
Our team did not want to focus much on existing analog locations, as those have been explored and researched deeply for years. The website we've created shows not only why the places that already have been operational have been chosen as the best to analog the conditions on moon and mars, and which indicator do they imitate best, but it also opens opportunities for new, un-researched locations to pop up backed by existing data. 
The project aims to find new analog places on earth, but with it come many more opportunities. Firstly, it summarizes data in one place, making it easier to check how well a given analog location used on earth will imitate conditions in different places on mars' surface. Also, besides the scientific role, it may be used in education, as it is approachable by a non-educated user to get to know martian and lunar conditions better.
We've also made a film about the project, linked below:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PW-tIyeIDBE
details:
Our project is a website that will determine a set of best analogue locations on earth for a given location on the moon or mars and other input data (time in a lunar/martian year/day, Values of Importace (VoI's)), using a custom made programme. The programme works in three steps.

1. The programme checks values of every indicator for a chosen point and date on mars surface in a compressed dataset made with data from NASA databases.

2. The programme calculates differences between values of the point and all points on earth each month, using a system that gives ranges to indicators values, and then plugs in the data to the similarity formula. This gives a parameter similarity mask for entire earth.

3. The programme uses an averageing method to calculate the final mask of the best analogs using weights provided by the user. We then return places with the highest scores.

This makes the programme customizable to meet the needs of users in the largest way possible. With an easy to understand interface it is usable by users of all kind of knowledge and goals.

The project is aimed not only to help in testing equipment, but to spark curiosity into minds of young people, who can use the website educationally. We're hoping that the influence of the project will be felt in years to come, with the new generations growing more engaged with space exploration.

The project has been made with:


  • Python42.9%
  • PHP27.8%
  • HTML18.4%
  • CSS5.5%
  • Shell3.2%
  • JavaScript2%
  • Dockerfile0.2%

with codes linked above. Also, we've used:

- Google Cloud;

- VScode;

- Anthropic - Claude;

- Google - Gemini;

- GitHub - https://github.com/VanClomp/nasa-project.git

We've did our best to process and collect the data in an approachable way, one, that those weren't shown before. To accomplish that, we've used our own ideas and came up with our own indicators.
